Instructions

OneLock looks exactly like your locked iPhone. Your spectator's guesses fail, but every code is secretly remembered, and then any code unlocks it.

Part 1: Setting up

Do this once, before you perform.

  1. Add it to your Home Screen. Open the link in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Always open it from that icon so it fills the screen.
  2. Open these settings. Tap the faint gear just above the bar at the bottom of the lock screen, or double-tap "Emergency" on the passcode keypad. The screen flips around. Tap Done to flip back.
  3. Add your home screens. Take screenshots of your real home screen pages and add them under Your Home Screens. Until you do, the built-in ones are used.
  4. Pick a wallpaper. Choose a built-in one or your own lock screen photo under Wallpaper.
  5. Stay away from the edges. Swiping in from the very edges of the screen is handled by the real iPhone, not OneLock. A swipe up from the bottom edge can close the app, and a swipe down from the top edge opens your iPhone's notifications. Start your swipes a little in from the edges, and keep an eye on your spectator's swipes too.

Part 2: Performing

It starts on the lock screen with the live time.

  1. Swipe up from the middle of the screen. The passcode keypad appears, just like a real iPhone.
  2. Set the number of digits if needed: hold any number from 1 to 9 for 1 second. The dots change to match. Or set it here under Passcode Length.
  3. Let them guess. Hand them the phone, and ask them to type a code. Each code shakes and fails like a real iPhone, and is secretly remembered.
  4. Make it unlock. Pick one of these:
    Double-tap "Cancel" whenever you like. The dots blink once, and the next code anyone types unlocks it. Double-tap again to turn it off (the dots blink longer).
    Automatic Unlock in settings: the phone unlocks by itself on the try you choose. Example: with try 3, the first two codes fail and the third one unlocks. Your own tries count too.

Part 3: Reading their codes

After it unlocks, the codes are hidden in plain sight.

  1. Look at the red numbers on the dock icons. Read them left to right, 2 digits per icon. The page dots and dock stay still while the pages swipe, just like a real iPhone.
    Zeros always show, so no digits are missed. For example, 1005 shows as 10 and 05.
  2. See the other codes. Double-tap anywhere on a home page and the badges switch to the next remembered code. It loops back around. All codes, including the one that unlocked, are also listed here under Remembered Codes.

Part 4: Resetting

  1. Lock it again. On a home page, put your finger in the space just above the top row of apps and slide down, or hold your finger still anywhere for 1 second. The lock screen slides back down.
  2. That's it. Locking turns the unlock off, ready for the next person. All the codes are still listed under Remembered Codes in settings until the next person types a code.

Secret controls

Lock screenSwipe up for the keypad
Number keyHold 1s to set the number of dots
CancelDouble-tap: any code unlocks (again to turn off)
Lock screen gearTap: open settings
EmergencyDouble-tap: open settings
Keypad, empty spotHold 1s: back to the lock screen
Home pageDouble-tap: show the next code
Home pageSlide down from just above the top row of apps, or hold 1s: lock and reset

Before you perform

  • Opened from the Home Screen icon, not from Safari
  • Swipes start away from the edges of the screen
  • Your own home screen screenshots added
  • Passcode length matches your real iPhone
  • Phone locked, so it starts fresh
